candidates.change_summary: Delete the require condition in the modifier onlyOwner, so anyone can call withdrawAll and drain funds.
Change withdrawAll to withdraw a fixed zero amount instead of the full balance, causing no transfer and differing behavior.
Replace the argument to withdraw with a constant 1 wei instead of the full balance, so the transferred amount differs.
Replace the recipient with a non-payable address to cause the transfer to always revert, making withdraw observable difference in revert/no-revert behavior.
Replace transfer with an empty block so that no ETH is sent, changing the subsequent ETH balance.
Replace the transferred amount with zero so that no ETH is sent despite the input, changing balance.
Delete the onlyOwner modifier so that non-owner can call withdraw and change the contract balance.
Delete the require statement in the modifier, allowing any caller to pass the guard and alter withdrawal behavior.
Replace the condition with true so that any caller passes, opening withdraw to non-owners.
Replace 'owner' with a zero address constant so non-owner can never pass, causing withdraw to always revert (observable difference from P).
Replace the entire body of sendMoney to return without sending funds, making _value remain in the contract so balance/withdrawable funds differ.
Remove the require statement from the modifier, allowing anyone to call sendMoney, which can alter balance via unauthorized withdrawals.

Replace the require check on the call result with a constant true, allowing sendMoney to succeed even when the external call fails, which changes the state of the target/contract if the call would have reverted.
Change the call in sendMoney to send zero wei instead of _value, affecting the balance transferred and possibly the success condition.
Use delegatecall instead of call, which executes target code in the context of C, potentially changing C's own balance and storage after sendMoney.
Remove the require statement after the external call so that sendMoney does not revert on failure, leaving contract state unchanged but the call still attempted.
